passage: Simran, come here, sit. Your brother told me you'll only let his friend play with your cycle if he gives you his stickers. Let your Mummy tell you something. subtopic: Kohlberg self-interest stage

passage: On the school trip to the zoo, it started raining hard, and only Tanvir had brought an umbrella. Pintu, his classmate, was getting soaked. She crouched and said, "Tanvir, that's clever bargaining. But look at Pintu. He's cold. How would you feel if you were wet and nobody shared unless you paid?" qa.a: She praised his cleverness instead of shaming him, then asked him to imagine being wet and alone, which turned his attention to Pintu's feelings.

qa.q: How might Pintu feel when Tanvir says 'Keep your chips'?
qa.a: Pintu likely feels relieved and cared for, which is why he later shares his chips freely.

grounding: A teacher asks a child how he would feel if nobody shared without payment, moving him from a deal to care without shaming him.
